The organ is very old. Already in ancient Greece there was a water organ, the **hydraulis**. In the Middle Ages the organ came into the churches. Since then it has become ever larger and more refined. Because of its size and its many sounds it is called the **“king of instruments”**. Organ builders are craftsmen who build each organ individually for a particular space.

gewusst: The lowest organ pipes produce notes that one almost feels more than hears.
Organ building and organ music in Germany have belonged to UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage since 2017.

teile.einleitung: Methodism is a Protestant movement that arose in England in the 18th century. It was founded by the priest John Wesley. Today there are Methodist churches all over the world, also in Switzerland.
wichtigste: John Wesley is regarded as the founder of Methodism.
Methodism emerged from the Anglican Church, the Church of England.
The name comes from the regulated, methodical life of the first members.
John Wesley often preached in the open air.
His brother Charles Wesley wrote over 6,000 hymns.
In Switzerland the Methodist church is called the Evangelisch-methodistische Kirche (EMK, Evangelical Methodist Church).

abschnitte.text: In Oxford, around 1729, students gathered around the brothers **John and Charles Wesley**. They lived by strict rules: they prayed regularly, read the Bible and helped the poor and prisoners. Other students made fun of them and called them **Methodists**, because they lived so methodically. The nickname later became the name of a whole church.

**John Wesley** lived from 1703 to 1791 and was a priest of the Anglican Church. Many churches would not let him into the pulpit with his new way of preaching. So he gave **field sermons** in the open air, for example to miners and workers. In this way he reached people who rarely went to church. Wesley travelled on horseback through the country all his life and preached tens of thousands of times.

His brother **Charles Wesley** wrote over 6,000 church hymns. The hymns helped people to understand the faith and to celebrate together. Many of them are still sung in English-speaking churches today. Singing together is still an important part of Methodist services.

For Methodists, **faith and social action** belong together. Wesley already cared for the sick, prisoners and the poor. He sharply criticised **slavery**. Wesley remained an Anglican priest all his life. Only after his death did the Methodists separate completely from the Church of England and form their own churches, especially in America too.

In the 19th century Methodist preachers also came to Switzerland. Today the Methodists here are organised in the **Evangelisch-methodistische Kirche (EMK)**. It belongs to the worldwide **United Methodist Church**. The EMK is a free church and works with other churches, for example in diaconal organisations that help people in need.

gewusst: John Wesley is said to have covered hundreds of thousands of kilometres on horseback in his life.
A well-known Christmas carol in English, “Hark! The Herald Angels Sing”, comes from Charles Wesley.

teile.einleitung: “Lamb of God” is an important Christian image for Jesus. The gentle lamb stands for innocence and for the fact that Jesus gave his life for human beings.
wichtigste: In the Bible Jesus is called “Lamb of God”.
John the Baptist first called Jesus this.
A lamb is a young sheep and stands for gentleness and innocence.
In Latin it is “Agnus Dei”, which is also the name of a chant in the Mass.
The Paschal lamb often carries a flag with a cross.
Jesus also calls himself the good shepherd.

abschnitte.text: A **lamb** is a young sheep. It is regarded as gentle and peaceful. A lamb does not fight back and does no harm to anyone. That is why in Christian art it stands for **gentleness** and **innocence**. Sheep were very important animals in the time of Jesus, and many people knew them well.

In the **Gospel of John**, **John the Baptist** sees Jesus coming and says: “Behold, the Lamb of God.” In this he recalls the **Passover lamb**, which the Jews ate in remembrance of the liberation from Egypt. Christians see in Jesus a lamb who gives his life for human beings. In the last book of the Bible, **Revelation**, too, Jesus is often described as a lamb.

In Latin “Lamb of God” is **“Agnus Dei”**. “Agnus” means lamb, and “Dei” means of God. This is also the name of a chant in the **Mass** that is sung before communion. Many famous composers have set the “Agnus Dei” to music. In the English version people sing “Lamb of God, you take away the sins of the world”.

In pictures the **Paschal lamb** often carries a white **flag with a red cross**. The flag is a sign of victory over death. At Easter people also bake a cake in the shape of a lamb. It is often sprinkled with **icing sugar** and sometimes decorated with a little flag.

In the Gospel of John, Jesus says: “I am the **good shepherd**.” A good shepherd cares for his sheep, seeks the lost ones and protects them. Christians sometimes see themselves as sheep whom Jesus looks after. That is why in some churches pastors are also called shepherds or pastoral carers.

gewusst: The word “pastor” comes from Latin and means shepherd.
On the Ghent Altarpiece in Belgium there is a famous picture of the Adoration of the Lamb.

teile.einleitung: The conclave is the assembly of the cardinals that elects a new Pope. It takes place in the Vatican in Rome, behind closed doors in the Sistine Chapel.
wichtigste: In the conclave the cardinals elect a new Pope.
Only cardinals under 80 years old may vote.
A candidate needs two thirds of the votes.
White smoke and the ringing of bells show that a Pope has been elected.
With “Habemus Papam” the new Pope is announced.
In May 2025 Leo XIV was elected, the first Pope from the USA.

abschnitte.text: The word **conclave** comes from Latin and means roughly “with a key”. During the election the cardinals are shut off from the outside world. They may have no contact with the outside. The vote is held in the **Sistine Chapel** in the Vatican. A conclave takes place when a Pope dies or resigns.

The **cardinals** are appointed by the Pope. They advise him and, after his death or resignation, elect his successor. Only cardinals who are not yet **80 years** old may vote. In May 2025, **133 cardinals** from about 70 countries took part in the vote, more than ever before.

Each cardinal writes a name on a ballot paper. A candidate needs the votes of **two thirds** of those voting. After the rounds of voting the ballot papers are burned in a stove. **Black smoke** means: no Pope yet. **White smoke** means: a Pope has been elected. In addition the **bells of St Peter's Basilica** ring, so that nobody misunderstands the signal.

After the election a cardinal steps out onto the balcony of St Peter's Basilica and calls **“Habemus Papam”**, which means “We have a Pope”. Then he names the person elected and the papal name that he has chosen. On 8 May 2025 Cardinal Robert Francis Prevost was elected. He called himself **Leo XIV** and is the first Pope from the **USA**.

gewusst: In the Middle Ages a papal election once lasted almost three years, which is why strict rules for shutting the cardinals in were introduced.
During the time without a Pope, the Swiss Guard in the Vatican also provides security.

teile.einleitung: The creation story stands right at the beginning of the Bible, in the first Book of Moses. It tells how God creates the world in six days and rests on the seventh day.
wichtigste: On the first day God created light.
On the second day he made the sky.
On the third day the first plants grew.
On the fourth day came the sun, moon and stars, on the fifth fish and birds.
On the sixth day God created human beings in his own image.
On the seventh day God rested and found everything very good.

abschnitte.text: The Bible begins with the words: “In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.” At first everything was dark and empty. On the **first day** God said: “Let there be light.” So he separated the **light** from the darkness, day from night. On the **second day** he made the **sky**, which separates the waters above from the waters below.

On the **third day** the water gathered together and dry land appeared. Then the first **plants** grew: grass, herbs and trees with fruit. On the **fourth day** God set the **sun, moon and stars** in the sky. They were to give light and to mark days, months and years.

On the **fifth day** God filled the water with **fish** and the sky with **birds**. On the **sixth day** he created the land animals. Then God created **human beings in his own image**. This means that people are like God in a special way and are meant to look after the earth. In the end God looked at everything and found it **very good**.

On the **seventh day** God rested from his work. That is why the Sabbath is a **day of rest** for Jews and Sunday for Christians. Many people do not understand the story as a scientific report. They see in it a story that says: the world is wanted, ordered and good.

gewusst: Right at the start, the Bible contains two different creation stories; the second tells of Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden.
Our week of seven days is closely connected with this story.

teile.einleitung: Conrad Grebel was a man from Zurich who lived at the time of the Reformation. He is regarded as one of the founders of the Anabaptist movement, from which the Mennonites and the Amish later emerged.
wichtigste: Conrad Grebel came from a respected Zurich family.
At first he supported Zwingli, then he broke with him.
He rejected infant baptism: baptism should presuppose a personal confession of faith.
On 21 January 1525 he baptised Georg Blaurock in Zurich.
With this the Anabaptist movement began.
He died as early as 1526 of the plague.

abschnitte.text: Conrad Grebel was born around 1498 and came from a distinguished **Zurich family**. His father sat on the city council. Grebel studied in Basel, Vienna and Paris and learned Latin and Greek. Back in Zurich he joined the Reformer **Huldrych Zwingli** and read the Bible with him and others.

Grebel and his friends found that **infant baptism** had no basis in the Bible. Only people who confess their faith themselves should be baptised. They wanted a congregation of conscious believers, separate from the authorities. Zwingli and the Zurich council rejected this. In 1524 Grebel and friends wrote a letter to **Thomas Müntzer**. In it he rejected violence and urged defencelessness.

On **21 January 1525** Grebel and his friends met in a private house in Zurich. The former priest **Georg Blaurock** asked Grebel to baptise him on his confession of faith. After that Blaurock baptised the others present. This day is regarded as the beginning of the **Anabaptist movement**. The authorities persecuted the Anabaptists, and Grebel was arrested. He managed to escape and died in 1526 of the plague.

The Anabaptists were persecuted in many countries. Even so, their movement spread in Europe and later in North America. Today **Mennonites**, **Amish** and **Hutterites** are among their best-known descendants. Many of them still reject violence and military service. In Switzerland too there are still Anabaptist congregations, for example in the Emmental and in the Jura.

gewusst: The Anabaptists were so called because they baptised adults again; they themselves preferred to speak of believers' baptism.
In 2004 the Reformed Church of the canton of Zurich officially asked the Anabaptists for forgiveness for the earlier persecution.

teile.einleitung: Hospital chaplains accompany sick people, their relatives and the staff in the hospital. They listen, help with worries and questions about meaning, and pray when that is wanted. In Switzerland they often work on behalf of the regional churches.
wichtigste: Hospital chaplaincy accompanies patients and relatives in difficult times.
In many Swiss hospitals, Reformed and Catholic chaplains work together ecumenically.
Chaplaincy is open to everyone, including people with no religious affiliation.
Conversations are protected by professional secrecy under Art. 321 of the Criminal Code.
“Spiritual care” means attending to the spiritual needs of sick people.
In 2015 the first professorship for spiritual care in Switzerland was created at the University of Zurich.

abschnitte.text: Anyone who lies sick in hospital often has many questions and worries. **Hospital chaplains** visit people at the bedside, listen and take time. They talk about fears, hopes and questions of meaning. If asked, they pray, bless or hold a service. **Relatives** and hospital staff can also turn to them.

In many Swiss hospitals, chaplaincy is organised **ecumenically**. Reformed and Catholic chaplains work in a joint team. They visit people of every background and every religion, including those with no denomination. Nobody is converted; it is about accompanying people. In some hospitals there are also chaplains from other religious communities.

What you confide in a chaplain stays secret. Professional secrecy under **Art. 321 of the Criminal Code** counts clergy among the professions bound to confidentiality, like doctors and lawyers. Anyone who betrays a confided secret can be punished. That is why patients can speak openly. This trust is very important for chaplaincy.

Today people in healthcare often speak of **spiritual care**. It means attending to the spiritual needs of sick people, that is, meaning, hope and faith. Chaplains work with doctors and nurses in doing so. On 1 October 2015, the first professorship for spiritual care in Switzerland was created at the Faculty of Theology of the **University of Zurich**. It was funded by the Catholic and Reformed churches in the canton of Zurich. The first professor was the theologian **Simon Peng-Keller**, who also teaches medical students.

gewusst: Many hospitals have a quiet room in which people of any religion can find peace.
The Zurich professorship for spiritual care was at first limited to six years.

teile.einleitung: In infant baptism a baby or small child is received into the Christian church. Baptism is one of the most important signs in Christianity. The family, godmother and godfather and the congregation celebrate it together in the service.
wichtigste: Baptism is done with water.
People baptise in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.
Usually water is poured three times over the head.
Godmother and godfather promise to accompany the child.
The christening gown is usually white.
The person baptised receives a baptismal candle.
You can be baptised at any age.

abschnitte.text: At baptism the child is baptised **with water**. Usually the pastor pours a little water **three times** over the head. In doing so the pastor speaks the child's name and says: “I baptise you **in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit**.” The water is a sign of new life and cleansing. For this there is often a **font** in the church.

In Switzerland the godparents are called **Gotti** (godmother) and **Götti** (godfather) in dialect. They **promise** to **accompany** the child on its path through life. They are also meant to help it get to know the faith. For many children, godmother and godfather are important people their whole life long. Often they give a special present on the birthday.

The **christening gown** is usually **white**. White is the colour of joy and of a new beginning. Some families pass a christening gown on from generation to generation. The person baptised also receives a **baptismal candle**. It is lit from the Paschal candle and recalls Jesus as the light of the world.

**The family and the congregation** celebrate baptism together in the service. The child is thereby received into the **community of the Church**. The congregation often promises to help support the child. After the service the family usually celebrates together as well. You can celebrate the day of baptism every year as a little feast day.

Many children are baptised when they are still babies. The parents then decide for them. But you can be baptised **at any age**, even as a teenager or **adult**. In some free churches only people who can decide for themselves are baptised. In the Reformed churches, young people later confirm their baptism at **confirmation**.

gewusst: Baptism is mutually recognised by almost all Christian churches.
At the font of many old churches, children from the whole village were baptised over the centuries.

teile.einleitung: The Sonderbund War of 1847 was the last war on Swiss soil. Seven Catholic-conservative cantons faced the liberal cantons of the Federal Diet. After the short war, the modern federal state was founded in 1848.
wichtigste: The Sonderbund was an alliance of Catholic-conservative cantons.
It included Lucerne, Uri, Schwyz, Obwalden and Nidwalden, Zug, Fribourg and Valais.
The closure of the Aargau monasteries in 1841 and the call of the Jesuits to Lucerne in 1844 sharpened the dispute.
General Guillaume-Henri Dufour led the troops of the Federal Diet.
In November 1847 the war lasted barely four weeks.
Afterwards, the Swiss federal state was created in 1848.

abschnitte.text: In the first half of the 19th century, Switzerland was a loose union of cantons. The **liberals** wanted a stronger federal state and more freedoms. The **Catholic conservatives** wanted to preserve the rights of the cantons and the influence of the Church. In 1841 the canton of **Aargau** closed its monasteries. Many Catholics saw this as a breach of the Federal Pact, and the Aargau monastery dispute poisoned the atmosphere.

In 1844 the canton of **Lucerne** called the **Jesuits** to its higher schools. For liberals and radicals, the Jesuits were a sign of a pro-Rome policy that was hostile to progress. In 1844 and 1845, radical volunteers tried to overthrow the Lucerne government by force. These **volunteer expeditions** failed. They strengthened the Catholic cantons in their resolve to band together.

In 1845 seven cantons founded the **Sonderbund**: Lucerne, Uri, Schwyz, Obwalden and Nidwalden, Zug, Fribourg and Valais. Not all Catholic cantons took part. **Solothurn** was mostly Catholic but was governed by liberals and stood on the side of the Federal Diet. In 1847 the **Federal Diet**, the assembly of the cantons, declared the Sonderbund incompatible with the Federal Pact and decided to dissolve it.

The troops of the Federal Diet were led by the Geneva general **Guillaume-Henri Dufour**. He ordered that the wounded and prisoners be treated with care. The commander of the Sonderbund army was **Johann Ulrich von Salis-Soglio** from the Grisons, a Protestant. This shows that the conflict was not only about religion but also about politics. The war lasted from 3 to 29 November 1847, and in the end Valais surrendered. The losses remained comparatively small.

abschnitte.titel: The road to the federal state
abschnitte.text: After the victory of the Federal Diet, a new **Federal Constitution** was drawn up. It came into force in 1848 and made Switzerland a **federal state**. There was now a common government, the Federal Council, and a parliament with the National Council and the Council of States. The cantons kept many rights of their own, however. The balance between the Confederation and the cantons shapes Switzerland to this day.

gewusst: Dufour later also had the first accurate map of Switzerland produced, the Dufour Map.
The highest peak in Switzerland, the Dufourspitze, is named after General Dufour.

teile.einleitung: The St Matthew Passion is a great work of church music by Johann Sebastian Bach. With choirs, soloists and orchestra it tells of the suffering and death of Jesus. To this day it is performed above all in the time before Easter.
wichtigste: Johann Sebastian Bach composed the St Matthew Passion as Thomaskantor in Leipzig.
The first performance was on Good Friday, 11 April 1727, in the Thomaskirche in Leipzig.
The text follows chapters 26 and 27 of the Gospel of Matthew.
A tenor sings the narrative as the Evangelist, and a bass sings the words of Jesus.
The work is written for two choirs and two orchestras.
Felix Mendelssohn Bartholdy performed the Passion again in Berlin in 1829.

abschnitte.text: The word **Passion** comes from the Latin word for suffering. A Passion is a musical work about the story of Jesus's suffering, from his arrest to his death on the cross. Such works used to be sung at the service on **Good Friday**. On this day Christians remember the death of Jesus. Bach wrote several Passions; the St John Passion and the St Matthew Passion survive.

From 1723 Johann Sebastian Bach was **Thomaskantor** in Leipzig. He was responsible for the music in the main churches of the city and taught the Thomaner, the boys' choir. The St Matthew Passion was heard for the first time in 1727 in the **Thomaskirche**. The work lasts about three hours and has two parts. At the service there was a sermon between the two parts.

The **Evangelist** is a tenor. He delivers the biblical text, mostly in so-called **recitatives**, that is, in singing close to speech. The words of Jesus are sung by a bass, often accompanied by a soft sound of the strings. In the **arias** soloists reflect on what is happening, for example in the well-known aria “Have mercy, my God”. The choirs play now the crowd, now they speak for the congregation.

Bach divided the musicians into **two choirs and two orchestras**. In this way the groups can ask and answer questions, as in a conversation. In the mighty opening chorus a further voice with a well-known church hymn joins in. Again and again **chorales** are heard, plain church hymns that the congregation knew. The chorale “O Sacred Head, Sore Wounded” by Paul Gerhardt occurs five times.

After Bach's death his music fell almost into oblivion for a long time. In 1829 the only 20-year-old **Felix Mendelssohn Bartholdy** conducted a shortened version with the Sing-Akademie in Berlin. The performance was a great success. With it the **Bach revival** began, the rediscovery of Bach's works. Today choirs perform the St Matthew Passion all over the world, also in many Swiss churches and concert halls.

gewusst: The St Matthew Passion lasts about three hours and is among Bach's longest works.
The text of the arias and free choruses was written by the Leipzig poet Picander.

teile.einleitung: The feeding of the five thousand is a well-known miracle story from the Bible. With only five loaves and two fish, thousands of people are fed. The story is in all four Gospels.
wichtigste: There are only five loaves and two fish.
Jesus thanks God, blesses the bread and has it handed out.
About five thousand men are fed, as well as women and children.
Afterwards twelve baskets full of leftovers remain.
In the Gospel of John a boy brings five barley loaves.
The story is in all four Gospels.

abschnitte.text: Many people have followed Jesus to hear him. Evening is coming, and everyone is **hungry**. In the Gospel of John, Jesus asks the disciple **Philip** where bread can be bought. Philip says that even a lot of money would not be enough. The disciples do not know how to feed so many people.

There are only **five loaves** and **two fish**. In the Gospel of John, **Andrew** says that a little **boy** has them with him. They are **barley loaves**, a simple bread of poor people. For so many people it is far too little. Even so, Jesus has the people sit down in groups on the green grass.

Jesus takes the loaves and fish and looks up to heaven. He **gives thanks to God** and blesses the food. Then he breaks the bread and has the disciples hand it out. Everyone eats and is **satisfied**. The Bible mentions about **5,000 men**; according to Matthew, women and children were there as well.

After the meal the disciples gather up the leftover pieces. There are **twelve baskets** full. So there is more left over than there was at the beginning. The number twelve recalls the twelve tribes of Israel and the twelve disciples. In this way the story shows that with God there is enough for everyone.

The feeding of the five thousand is found in **Matthew, Mark, Luke and John**. It is one of the few miracles that all four Gospels tell. Matthew and Mark also report a second feeding, in which four thousand people are fed. Many Christians also see in the story a pointer to the **Lord's Supper**, in which bread is shared.

gewusst: In Tabgha on the Sea of Galilee there is a church with an old mosaic showing a basket of loaves and two fish.
Bread and fish were among the most common foods on the Sea of Galilee.

teile.einleitung: The Paschal (Easter) candle is a large, decorated candle that stands in many churches. It is lit for the first time in the Easter night. Its light is a sign of Jesus Christ, who according to the belief of Christians rose from the dead.
wichtigste: The new Paschal candle is lit in the Easter night from the Easter fire.
On the candle there are a cross, the letters Alpha and Omega and the year.
Alpha and Omega mean beginning and end.
Five red nails recall the wounds of Jesus.
Traditionally the Paschal candle is made of beeswax.
At a baptism the baptismal candle is lit from the Paschal candle.

abschnitte.text: In the night before Easter Sunday many churches celebrate the **Easter Vigil**. In front of the church an **Easter fire** is lit and blessed. From it the new **Paschal candle** is lit. Then it is carried into the dark church. The priest or deacon calls out three times **“Christ, the light”**, in Latin “Lumen Christi”. The congregation answers “Thanks be to God”.

On the candle a large **cross** can be seen. It recalls the death and resurrection of Jesus. Above and below it stand the Greek letters **Alpha and Omega**. Alpha is the first and Omega the last letter in the Greek alphabet. They mean: Christ is the **beginning and the end** of everything. In addition there is the **current year**, for every year there is a new candle.

Into the cross **five red nails** or grains of incense are often pressed. They stand for the wounds on the hands, feet and side of Jesus. Traditionally the Paschal candle is made of **beeswax**. Pure beeswax was regarded as especially precious. In an old chant of the Easter night, the **Exsultet**, even the bees that made the wax are praised.

In Eastertide the candle burns at every service. After that it often stands by the **baptismal font**. At a **baptism** the baptismal candle is lit from the Paschal candle. In this way the light is passed on to the child. At funerals too the Paschal candle is often lit, as a sign of hope.

gewusst: Many parishes have their Paschal candle newly decorated every year, sometimes by children.
In the Easter night the faithful pass the light on from candle to candle until the whole church is bright.

teile.einleitung: The Zurich Disputations were public debates about the faith in 1523. The Zurich council invited people to them so that Zwingli could defend his teaching. They were an important step for the Reformation in Zurich.
wichtigste: The First Zurich Disputation took place on 29 January 1523 in the town hall.
Johannes Fabri spoke for the Bishop of Constance.
The city council decided that Zwingli could go on preaching.
In October 1523 the Second Disputation dealt with images and the Mass.
At Easter 1525 the Reformed Lord's Supper was introduced.
The Catholic cantons regarded the Baden Disputation of 1526 as a victory.

abschnitte.text: Even in 1522 there was a quarrel about the faith in Zurich. During Lent, friends ate sausages in the house of the printer **Christoph Froschauer**, although meat was forbidden. This is called the **sausage meal**. Zwingli was present and afterwards defended the break with his work “On the Choice and Freedom of Foods”. The mood in the city grew ever more tense.

The Zurich council invited clergy from the city and the countryside for **29 January 1523**. The meeting took place in the **town hall**, not in a church. **Zwingli** was to defend his teaching before clergy and councillors. For this he had written 67 theses, the Conclusions. **Johannes Fabri** spoke for the Bishop of Constance. He refused to decide questions of faith in a city assembly.

In the end the **Council of the City of Zurich** decided. Zwingli could go on preaching, and all preachers were to keep to **Scripture**, that is, the Bible. In this way a worldly authority took over the decision in questions of faith. At that time this was something very new.

In **October 1523** the **Second Zurich Disputation** followed. Now it was about the veneration of **images** and the **Mass** as a sacrifice. The changes were carried out step by step afterwards. At **Easter 1525** the **Reformed Lord's Supper** was celebrated in the Grossmünster for the first time. Bread and wine were handed to the congregation at tables.

In 1526 another disputation took place in **Baden** in Aargau. Among those who debated there were **Johannes Eck** and **Johannes Oecolampadius**. Zwingli himself stayed away. The Catholic cantons regarded the result as a victory. The Confederation remained divided in questions of faith.

gewusst: At that time a large part of today's German-speaking Switzerland belonged to the diocese of Constance.
Zwingli's 67 theses are regarded as the first Reformed confession of faith in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Whoever no longer wishes to be a member of a national church can leave it. In Switzerland this is a right that protects freedom of belief. In recent decades more and more people have left.
wichtigste: You leave a national church with a written declaration.
In 2023 about 67,000 people left the Roman Catholic church.
From the Reformed church, almost 40,000 people left in 2023.
Many departures in autumn 2023 followed a study on serious misconduct in the church.
In 2022 the people with no denomination were for the first time a larger group than the Catholics.
A frequently mentioned reason is the church tax.
Around 1970 only about 1 per cent of the population had no denomination.

abschnitte.text: In Switzerland the Federal Constitution guarantees **freedom of belief and conscience**. Nobody has to belong to a religious community. Whoever wants to leave a **national church** sends a **written declaration** to the parish or to the responsible office. You do not have to give a reason. From the age of 16 you may decide about your religion yourself.

In **2023** **about 67,000 people** left the Roman Catholic church. That was more than ever before. From the Reformed church **almost 40,000** people left. There were especially many departures after **September 2023**. At that time a **study** by the University of Zurich appeared on serious misconduct by church people and on how the church had long kept silent about it.

People leave for various reasons. Some no longer believe in God or no longer feel connected to the church. Others disagree with the church's stance on certain questions. A frequently mentioned **financial reason** is the **church tax**. Whoever leaves no longer has to pay it.

abschnitte.titel: More and more with no denomination
abschnitte.text: Around **1970**, only **about 1 per cent** of the Swiss population had **no denomination**, that is, did not belong to any religious community. Since then this share has grown strongly. In **2022** the people with **no denomination** were for the first time a larger group than the **Catholics**. In the cantons of **Geneva** and **Vaud** there are hardly any counted departures. There there is **no formal membership with church tax** that one would have to leave.

gewusst: Whoever has left can join the church again later.
The figures on religion in Switzerland are collected regularly by the Federal Statistical Office with surveys.

teile.einleitung: The Two-Source Theory is an explanation from biblical scholarship. It explains why the Gospels of Matthew, Mark and Luke are so similar. According to it, Matthew and Luke used two sources: the Gospel of Mark and a collection of sayings called Q.
wichtigste: Matthew, Mark and Luke are called the Synoptic Gospels.
According to the theory, Mark is the oldest Gospel.
The second source is called the sayings source Q, from “Quelle”.
Q contains mainly words and speeches of Jesus.
Christian Hermann Weisse first formulated the theory in 1838.
Heinrich Julius Holtzmann helped it break through in 1863.

abschnitte.text: The Gospels of **Matthew**, **Mark** and **Luke** tell much of the story almost identically. They are called the **Synoptic Gospels** because they can be laid side by side and compared. Researchers asked how this similarity came about. The **Two-Source Theory** is the best-known answer.

According to the theory, **Mark** is the oldest Gospel. This is called **Markan priority**. Matthew and Luke used Mark as their first source. In addition there is a second source, the **sayings source Q**. The letter Q simply stands for the German word **Quelle**, source.

Q is reconstructed as a collection of **sayings** of Jesus, so-called logia. It contains mainly **words and speeches of Jesus**. According to today's reconstruction it contains no story of the Passion and Resurrection. An example is the **Lord's Prayer**: it is in Matthew and Luke but missing from Mark. Q is regarded as **hypothetical** because no manuscript of it survives.

**Christian Hermann Weisse** first formulated the theory in **1838**. Almost at the same time Christian Gottlob Wilke put forward Markan priority. **Heinrich Julius Holtzmann** gave it a thorough foundation in 1863 in his book “The Synoptic Gospels”. Afterwards it largely prevailed in German-language scholarship. In 1924 **Burnett Hillman Streeter** extended it into the **Four-Source Hypothesis**, with sources of their own, M and L.

Not all researchers are convinced. One objection is the **Minor Agreements**. These are small shared departures of Matthew and Luke from Mark. If both used Mark independently, they would hardly be likely to alter him in the same way. That is why there are other explanatory models as well.

gewusst: The word “synoptic” comes from Greek and means roughly “seeing together”.
Although Q has never been found, researchers have produced whole editions of its supposed text.

teile.einleitung: In Switzerland, state and Church are not connected in the same way everywhere. Recognition under public law gives certain religious communities a special status. Exactly what this looks like is decided by each canton itself.
wichtigste: According to Art. 72 of the Federal Constitution, the cantons regulate the relationship between Church and state.
That is why there are 26 different solutions in Switzerland.
The classic cantonal churches (Landeskirchen) are the Reformed, the Roman Catholic and in many places the Old Catholic Church.
Recognised churches are corporations under public law, but not part of the administration.
Church parishes (Kirchgemeinden) are democratically organised, and their members decide on the budget and the tax rate.
Freedom of belief and conscience (Art. 15 of the Federal Constitution) allows anyone to leave a church.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Constitution** says in Art. 72 that the **cantons** are responsible for the relationship between Church and state. That is why the situation is different in every canton. In many cantons certain churches are recognised as **Landeskirchen** (cantonal churches). In Geneva and Neuchâtel, by contrast, Church and state are largely separate. The Confederation takes care above all that religious freedom applies everywhere.

The classic cantonal churches are the **Evangelical Reformed**, the **Roman Catholic** and in many cantons the **Old Catholic** Church. They are **corporations under public law**. That means: they have their own legal personality and special rights, but do not belong to the state administration. Often they may levy a **church tax** on their members. In many cantons companies also pay such a tax.

Recognised **Kirchgemeinden** (church parishes) work in a similar way to political municipalities. The members elect their authorities and vote on the **budget** and the **tax rate**, at assemblies or at the ballot box. Among Catholics people speak of the **dual system**: alongside the diocese and the canonical parish (Pfarrei) there are church parishes and cantonal corporations under state law. These manage mainly money and staff in a democratic way.

Recognition is not reserved only for Christian churches. In the canton of **Zurich** the **Israelitische Cultusgemeinde** (Israelite Religious Community) and the Liberal Jewish Community are recognised under public law. The canton of **Basel-Stadt** additionally has a “small” cantonal recognition for communities organised under private law. An Alevi community, for example, has received it. It brings above all symbolic rights, but no power to tax.

Art. 15 of the Federal Constitution protects **freedom of belief and conscience**. Nobody may be forced to belong to a religious community, and anyone may leave. The relationship between Church and state changes again and again. In the canton of **Bern**, for example, pastors were employed by the canton until the end of 2019. Since the new Landeskirchengesetz (law on the cantonal churches) of 2020, the cantonal churches employ them themselves.

gewusst: In some cantons not only people but also companies pay church taxes, although companies cannot belong to a church.
Because every canton has its own rules, the church tax can change markedly just by moving to the neighbouring canton.

teile.einleitung: The Anabaptists were a movement of the Reformation period that began in Zurich. They baptised only people who believe for themselves and rejected the baptism of infants. For this they were persecuted for a long time, and many fled to the Jura or abroad.
wichtigste: The Anabaptists rejected the baptism of infants.
On 21 January 1525 the first adult baptism took place in Zurich.
Conrad Grebel was one of the founders of the movement.
Felix Manz was drowned in the Limmat in 1527.
The Schleitheim Articles of 1527 are an important confession of the Anabaptists.
The Amish are named after Jakob Ammann from Bern.

abschnitte.text: Most churches baptised even small children. The **Anabaptists**, by contrast, thought that only someone who believes in God for themselves and decides consciously should be baptised. That is why they baptised **adults**. Their opponents scornfully called them “re-baptisers”. They wanted a congregation of people who take their faith seriously.

**Conrad Grebel** was at first a follower of Zwingli. But he wanted a more radical Reformation. On **21 January 1525**, Grebel baptised **Georg Blaurock** in Zurich. This was the start of the Anabaptist movement. The Zurich council and the Reformed around Zwingli rejected the movement.

The Anabaptists were persecuted by the authorities because they did not fit into the order of the Church. **Felix Manz** was drowned in the **Limmat** on 5 January 1527. He was the first Anabaptist the Reformed put to death. Many Anabaptists therefore withdrew to remote areas such as the **Jura**. Others emigrated to Alsace, the Palatinate and later to **America**.

In 1527 Anabaptists wrote a confession in **Schleitheim** in the canton of Schaffhausen. It is called the **Schleitheim Articles** and came about under the leadership of **Michael Sattler**. In it the Anabaptists reject, for example, the **oath** and **military service**. They wanted to live as exactly as possible by the words of Jesus.

Various groups later grew out of the Anabaptists. The **Mennonites** are named after the Frisian Menno Simons. **Jakob Ammann** came from the Simmental in the canton of Bern. He split off in 1693, and his followers are called the **Amish**. Many Amish live in North America today and do without some modern technology.

gewusst: The Amish in America often still speak an old German dialect.
In Switzerland there are still Anabaptist congregations today, above all in the Emmental and in the Jura.

teile.einleitung: Liturgical colours are the colours of the vestments that priests and deacons wear in the service. Each colour belongs to a particular time in the church year or to a feast.
wichtigste: Purple belongs to Advent and Lent.
White or gold belongs to Christmas and Easter.
Red belongs to Pentecost, to martyrs' feasts and to Good Friday.
Green belongs to Ordinary Time.
Pink may be worn on two Sundays.
The stole shows the colour of the day.

abschnitte.text: The **church year** begins with Advent and has various seasons and feasts. With the **liturgical colours** the Church shows what is being celebrated at the moment. The colours can be seen on the vestments, on the **stole** and often also on the cloths at the altar. The rules apply above all in the Catholic Church, but many Protestant churches also know them.

**Purple** is the colour of preparation and reflection. It is worn in **Advent** and in **Lent**. On two Sundays the purple may be lightened to **pink**: on the third Sunday of Advent, called **Gaudete**, and on the fourth Sunday of Lent, called **Laetare**. Both names mean “Rejoice”. In this way pink shows the anticipation of Christmas and Easter.

**White** or **gold** stands for joy, light and purity. It belongs to the great feasts of Christ such as **Christmas** and **Easter**. **Green** stands for hope and growth. It is the colour of **Ordinary Time**, that is, the Sundays without a great feast. Because this time lasts longest, you see green in most weeks of the year.

**Red** recalls the **fire** of the Holy Spirit, who came down on the disciples at **Pentecost** like tongues of fire. Red is also the colour of **blood**. That is why priests wear it at the feasts of **martyrs**, who were killed because of their faith. Since the liturgical reform after the Second Vatican Council, red is also the colour of **Good Friday**, the day on which the suffering of Christ is remembered.

The **stole** is a narrow, long band of cloth. It belongs to the dress of ordained ministers. The **priest** wears it around the neck so that both ends hang down at the front. The **deacon** wears it diagonally across the left shoulder. The stole always has the colour of the day.

gewusst: At funerals priests usually wear purple, whereas in the past black was often customary.
Pink is worn on only two Sundays in the whole year and is therefore the rarest liturgical colour.

teile.einleitung: Predestination means “determining beforehand”. It refers to the teaching that God decided before all time which people will be saved. Best known is the form taught by the Reformer John Calvin in Geneva.
wichtigste: Predestination means determining beforehand.
Calvin taught double predestination: God destines some to salvation, others to damnation.
Calvin himself called the decree of rejection a “dreadful decree”.
The Synod of Dort in 1618/19 confirmed the strict teaching against the Arminians.
In 1904/05 Max Weber linked the teaching with the spirit of modern capitalism.

abschnitte.text: The Reformer **John Calvin** worked in **Geneva**. In his main work, the **“Institutes”**, he taught **double predestination**. According to it God has destined from eternity some people to salvation and the others to damnation. A person cannot earn salvation himself; it is by God's grace alone. Calvin himself called the decree of rejection a **“dreadful decree”**, because he felt it to be awe-inspiring and incomprehensible.

Not all Reformed Christians agreed. In the Netherlands the **Arminians**, named after Jacobus Arminius, taught that a person can freely respond to God's grace. The **Synod of Dort** in 1618/19 decided against them and confirmed the strict teaching. Envoys from Swiss Reformed places also took part in it.

The German sociologist **Max Weber** wrote in 1904/05 about the Protestant ethic and the spirit of capitalism. He suggested that many Calvinists looked for signs of whether they belonged to the elect. Diligence, thrift and success in one's profession could count as such signs. Weber's thesis is well known, but is still judged differently to this day.

gewusst: The word comes from the Latin “praedestinare”, to determine beforehand.
The Church Father Augustine had already thought about predestination long before Calvin.

teile.einleitung: The Church Fathers were important Christian scholars of the first centuries after Christ. They explained the faith, translated the Bible and shaped the teaching of the Church. Their writings are still read today.
wichtigste: The study of the Church Fathers is called patristics.
Jerome created the Latin Bible translation, the Vulgate.
Ambrose of Milan baptised Augustine in 387.
After the sack of Rome in 410, Augustine wrote “The City of God”.
John Chrysostom received the nickname “Golden Mouth”.
Basil, Gregory of Nazianzus and Gregory of Nyssa are called the Cappadocian Fathers.
In the “Hexapla”, Origen set six versions of the Old Testament side by side.

abschnitte.text: **Church Fathers** is the name for significant theologians of the **early Church**, roughly from the 2nd to the 8th century. They lived exemplary lives and their teaching was recognised by the Church. They wrote sermons, letters and books about the faith. The discipline that studies their life and work is called **patristics**. The word comes from the Latin “pater”, father.

In the West four are regarded as the great **Latin Church Fathers**: **Ambrose**, **Jerome**, **Augustine** and **Gregory the Great**. **Jerome** translated the Bible into Latin. This translation was later called the **Vulgate** and for over a thousand years was the most important Bible in the West. **Ambrose** was Bishop of **Milan**. Gregory the Great was Pope and promoted church singing.

**Augustine** was one of the most influential Church Fathers. He was baptised in Milan in **387** by **Ambrose**. Later he was Bishop of Hippo in North Africa. In the year **410** the **Visigoths** plundered the city of Rome. In answer Augustine wrote the work **“De civitate Dei”**, in English **“The City of God”**. Also well known are his “Confessions”, in which he tells of his life.

In the Greek-speaking East too there were great Church Fathers. **John Chrysostom** was Patriarch of **Constantinople**. Because of his skill in preaching he received the nickname **“Golden Mouth”**. **Basil**, **Gregory of Nazianzus** and **Gregory of Nyssa** lived in the 4th century in Cappadocia, in present-day Turkey. They are called the **Cappadocian Fathers**.

**Origen** was an early Christian scholar from **Alexandria** in Egypt. He lived in the 3rd century and wrote a great many works. In the **“Hexapla”** he set **six versions** of the Old Testament side by side in columns. The word means “sixfold”. In this way one could compare the Hebrew text and various Greek translations.

gewusst: The Vulgate was used in Catholic services until the 20th century.
Augustine is among the most widely read authors of antiquity.

teile.einleitung: The Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople is one of the oldest churches in the world. Its head is regarded as the honorary head of the Orthodox Christians. Its seat is still in Istanbul, the former Constantinople.
wichtigste: Since 1991 Bartholomew I has been Ecumenical Patriarch (as of 2026).
Since 1601 the seat has been in the Istanbul district of Phanar on the Golden Horn.
The main church is the Cathedral of St George.
The Council of 381 gave Constantinople the rank immediately after Rome.
In 1965 Athenagoras I and Pope Paul VI lifted the excommunications of 1054.
In 2019 the Orthodox Church of Ukraine received its independence (autocephaly).

abschnitte.text: In the 4th century Emperor Constantine made the city of Byzantium his capital, Constantinople. The **First Council of Constantinople** in **381** decided that its bishop has the rank of honour immediately after the **Bishop of Rome**. The reason given was that Constantinople was the “new Rome”. The Council of **Chalcedon** confirmed this in 451. Today the Patriarch is regarded as “first among equals” of the Orthodox churches.

In **1453** the Ottomans conquered Constantinople. The famous **Hagia Sophia**, formerly the church of the patriarchs, became a mosque. Sultan **Mehmed II** installed **Gennadius II Scholarius** as the first patriarch under Ottoman rule. The patriarch became head of all Orthodox subjects. Since **1601** the seat has been in the district of **Phanar** (Turkish Fener). The main church there is the **Cathedral of St George**.

In **1054** the churches of Rome and Constantinople had excommunicated each other. On **7 December 1965** Patriarch **Athenagoras I** and Pope **Paul VI** declared at the same time that they were lifting these excommunications. That was an important step of reconciliation between the Eastern and Western Church. Since then popes and patriarchs have met again and again.

**Bartholomew I** was elected in **1991**. He is the longest-serving Ecumenical Patriarch in history. Because he campaigns strongly for **environmental protection**, he is called the “green patriarch”. In January **2019** the Patriarchate granted the **Orthodox Church of Ukraine** **autocephaly**, that is, full independence. This led to a serious dispute within Orthodoxy.

The Patriarchate is also represented in Switzerland. In **Chambésy** near Geneva it founded the **Orthodox Centre** in **1966**. There, among other things, a great council of all Orthodox churches was prepared. This shows how important Geneva is as a place of encounter between the churches.

gewusst: The Patriarchate has had its seat in the same district of Istanbul for over 400 years.
After the district of Phanar, influential Greek families there were called “Phanariots”.

teile.einleitung: At a church wedding a couple celebrate their marriage in the church. The couple promise each other faithfulness before God and the congregation and ask for God's blessing. In Switzerland the civil ceremony at the registry office comes first.
wichtigste: The wedding celebration in church is also called the marriage service.
In Switzerland the couple must first go to the registry office.
Bride and groom say “Yes” to each other.
They exchange rings.
The round wedding ring stands for love without end.
The couple ask for God's blessing.
Witnesses are present as witnesses.

abschnitte.text: In Switzerland only the **civil ceremony** is legally valid. So a couple must first go **to the registry office**. There the marriage is officially concluded. Only after that may a **church wedding** take place. Many couples celebrate both on the same day or shortly one after the other.

At the wedding the pastor asks the couple whether they want to go through life together. Bride and groom answer with **“Yes”**. Then they **exchange** the **rings**. The round **wedding ring** has no beginning and no end. It is therefore a sign of **love without end** and of faithfulness.

At a church wedding **the couple ask for God's blessing** on their marriage. The pastor speaks the blessing over the two. There are also songs, prayers and a short sermon, often on a Bible text that the couple have chosen. A text by Paul about love is well known: “Love never ends.” In the Catholic Church marriage is regarded as a **sacrament**.

The **wedding dress** is usually **white**. At the wedding the **witnesses** are also present. They are friends or relatives who testify that the marriage was concluded. Often they also help with planning the celebration. When the couple come out of the church, the **church bells** often **ring**, and the guests offer their congratulations.

gewusst: The custom of wearing the wedding ring on the ring finger is very old.
A wedding ring often has an engraving inside with the names or the date of the wedding.

teile.einleitung: The Roman Catholic Church is the largest Christian church in the world. At its head stands the Pope in Rome. In Switzerland too it is one of the great churches.
wichtigste: The Pope leads the worldwide Church with the Roman Curia.
The cardinals elect a new Pope in the conclave.
In May 2025 Leo XIV was elected Pope.
The Pontifical Swiss Guard has protected the Pope since 1506.
In Switzerland there are six dioceses.
The Second Vatican Council took place from 1962 to 1965.

abschnitte.text: The head of the Church is the **Pope**, the Bishop of Rome. He lives in **Vatican City**, the smallest state in the world. To lead and administer the worldwide Church he has an authority: the **Roman Curia**. In **May 2025** **Leo XIV** was elected Pope, the first Pope from the USA.

The **cardinals** are important advisers of the Pope. On solemn occasions they wear **red**. When a Pope dies or resigns, they gather in the Sistine Chapel for the **conclave**. The word means “with a key”, because they vote shut in. White smoke from the chimney shows that a new Pope has been elected.

Since **1506** the **Pontifical Swiss Guard** has protected the Pope. Its members are young Catholic men with Swiss citizenship. On solemn occasions they wear colourful uniforms in blue, yellow and red. The Guard is one of the oldest troops still in existence in the world.

In Switzerland the Catholic Church is divided into **six dioceses**: Basel, Chur, Lausanne-Geneva-Fribourg, Lugano, St Gallen and Sion. At the head of a diocese stands a **bishop**. In addition there are two territorial abbeys. The bishops work together in the Swiss Bishops' Conference.

From **1962 to 1965** the **Second Vatican Council** took place. Bishops from all over the world discussed the renewal of the Church. Since then Mass may be celebrated in the local language instead of only in Latin. Catholic priests commit themselves to **celibacy**, so they do not marry.

gewusst: The Swiss Guard swears in new guardsmen every year on 6 May.
The word “catholic” comes from Greek and means all-embracing.

teile.einleitung: The church tax is a tax with which the members finance the recognised churches. In Switzerland the cantons decide whether and how it is levied. That is why the rules differ from canton to canton.
wichtigste: The cantons determine whether and how church taxes are levied.
The members of a recognised church have to pay.
It is often calculated as a percentage of the state tax.
In most cantons companies also pay church tax.
In Geneva the church tax is voluntary, and church and state have been separate since 1907.
Vaud finances the recognised churches from general taxes.
In most German federal states the church tax is 9 per cent of income tax.

abschnitte.text: In Switzerland the **cantons** regulate the relationship between state and church. So they also determine **whether and how church taxes are levied**. Usually the Reformed and the Roman Catholic churches are **recognised**, often also the Christ Catholic. In some cantons further communities are recognised. The tax is often levied by the **parishes**.

As a private person, only those who are **members of a recognised church** pay. Whoever leaves no longer has to pay church tax. In many cantons it is calculated as a **percentage of the state tax**. So whoever pays more tax also pays more church tax. Part of the money flows into **social services**, for example counselling, pastoral care, youth work or help for people in need.

In **most cantons** **companies**, that is, legal entities, also pay church tax. According to an overview by the tax authorities this is the case in **18 cantons**. This is controversial, because a company has no faith. The **Federal Supreme Court** nevertheless holds this tax to be constitutional. It justifies this by saying that **legal entities cannot appeal to freedom of belief**. In some cantons the companies' money may be used only for non-religious tasks.

In the canton of **Geneva**, church and state have been separate since **1907**. There the church tax is **voluntary**. The canton of **Vaud** has no church tax. It finances the recognised churches **from general taxes**. Neuchâtel also has a solution of its own, with a voluntary contribution.

In Germany too there is a church tax. In **most federal states** it is **9 per cent of income tax**. In Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg it is 8 per cent. The state collects the church tax there and passes it on to the churches.

gewusst: Without church tax many parishes would have to cut their services sharply.
On the tax bill the church tax usually appears together with the state and municipal tax.

teile.einleitung: The Waldensians are a Christian movement that arose in Lyon in the 12th century. Their founder Waldo lived in poverty and preached without the permission of the Church. After long persecution they joined the Reformation.
wichtigste: The founder was the merchant Waldo of Lyon.
His followers were also called the Poor of Lyon.
Waldo had parts of the Bible translated into the vernacular.
In 1184 the Waldensians were condemned as heretics at Verona.
In 1532 they joined the Reformation at the Synod of Chanforan.
In 1689 they returned from Switzerland to their valleys in Piedmont.

abschnitte.text: **Peter Waldo** was a rich merchant in **Lyon**. Around 1173 he gave up his possessions. From then on he lived as a **travelling preacher** in poverty. So that lay people could understand the faith better, he had parts of the Bible translated into the **vernacular** of his region. In this way even simple people could understand the Gospels and pass them on.

Waldo's followers gave up possessions and preached in pairs. After their city of origin they were called the **Poor of Lyon**. But they preached without the permission of the Church. That is why Pope **Lucius III** condemned them in 1184 at the **Synod of Verona** as heretics, that is, as teachers of false doctrine.

The Waldensians wanted to live entirely by the Bible. In the **Sermon on the Mount**, Jesus says one should not swear at all. The Waldensians took this literally and **refused oaths**. This often brought them into conflict with the authorities, because oaths were very important at that time. Many Waldensians withdrew to remote Alpine valleys in **Piedmont**.

In 1532 the Waldensians met at **Chanforan** in Piedmont. At this synod they decided to join the **Reformed** movement. The Reformer **Guillaume Farel** was also present. Since then the Waldensian Church has been a Protestant church.

In 1686 the Waldensians were driven from their valleys. Many found refuge in **Switzerland**. In 1689 about 900 armed men under **Henri Arnaud** returned to their homeland from Lake Geneva. This is called the **Glorious Return**. In February 1848, King Charles Albert granted the Waldensians in the Kingdom of Sardinia-Piedmont civil rights.

gewusst: The Waldensians still celebrate 17 February today as the day commemorating their equal rights.
The Waldensian Church is now one of the largest Protestant churches in Italy.

teile.einleitung: According to Christian belief, every person has a guardian angel who accompanies and protects them. Angels appear in many stories of the Bible and bring messages from God.
wichtigste: According to Christian belief, a guardian angel protects a person.
The word angel means messenger.
In pictures, angels usually have wings.
In the Bible angels often say: “Do not be afraid.”
In pictures the archangel Michael fights a dragon.
The feast of the guardian angels is on 2 October.

abschnitte.text: The word **angel** comes from the Greek “angelos” and means **messenger**. In the Bible, angels bring messages from God to people. Because people are often frightened, angels frequently say first: **“Do not be afraid.”** In pictures, angels usually have **wings**. They show that angels travel between heaven and earth.

According to Christian belief, every person has a **guardian angel**. It accompanies and **protects** them throughout their life. Many children say a guardian angel prayer in the evening **before falling asleep**. When someone has just escaped an accident, people say in everyday life: **They had a guardian angel.** The Catholic Church celebrates the **feast of the guardian angels on 2 October**.

Some angels have a name in the Bible. They are called **archangels**. In many pictures **Michael** fights a **dragon**, as a sign of the victory of good over evil. **Gabriel** brings important messages. According to the Book of Tobit, **Raphael** accompanied the young **Tobias** on his journey and protected him.

Angels can be seen everywhere in churches, in paintings and at Christmas. In the past they were painted as adults with large wings, later often as small children. Even people who are not religious like to give guardian angels as lucky charms, for example as pendants in the car.

gewusst: Raphael's name means “God heals” in Hebrew.
The archangel Michael is the patron saint of many churches, including in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The name day is a small feast celebrated on a particular day of the year. It is the feast day of the saint who bears the same first name. Name days are popular especially in Catholic and Orthodox regions.
wichtigste: On the name day one celebrates the feast day of the saint with the same name.
This saint is called the name patron.
Joseph has his name day on 19 March, Barbara on 4 December.
Valentine celebrates on 14 February, Stephen on 26 December.
Gallus, after whom St Gallen is named, has his feast day on 16 October.
Niklaus von Flüe is the national patron saint of Switzerland, and his feast day is on 25 September.

abschnitte.text: Many first names go back to **saints**. These are people who, according to the belief of the Church, led an especially good life. Every saint has a **feast day** in the calendar. Whoever has the same name has a **name day** on that day. The saint is then the **name patron**. He is meant to be a model and, according to belief, to watch over the person.

Saint **Joseph**, the husband of Mary, has his feast day on **19 March**. Saint **Barbara** is celebrated on **4 December**. On this day people put branches in water that are supposed to blossom at Christmas. Valentine's Day on **14 February** is the day of Saint **Valentine**. Saint **Anne**, according to tradition the mother of Mary, has her name day on **26 July**.

St Stephen's Day on **26 December** is a public holiday in many cantons. The monk **Gallus** lived on the river Steinach. The city and canton of **St Gallen** are named after him, and his feast day is 16 October. **Niklaus von Flüe** lived as a hermit in the Ranft in Obwalden. He is the national patron saint of Switzerland, and his feast day is on **25 September**.

In the past, in Catholic regions the name day was often **more important than the birthday**. People received small presents, flowers or a cake. Today many people celebrate mainly the birthday. In some countries, for example in Poland or Greece, however, the name day is still a big celebration. Some names have several saints and therefore several possible name days.

gewusst: In some countries the name days are printed in every calendar so that nobody is forgotten.
Whoever bears a name without a saint can choose a name patron with a similar name.

teile.einleitung: Meister Eckhart was a monk, preacher and thinker in the Middle Ages. He is among the best-known Christian mystics. Mystics seek a wholly inward, personal union with God.
wichtigste: Meister Eckhart lived from about 1260 to 1328.
He belonged to the Dominican order.
He wrote learned works in Latin, and gave his sermons in Middle High German.
Important ideas in his thought are detachment, the little spark of the soul and the birth of God in the soul.
In 1329 Pope John XXII condemned propositions from his work with the bull “In agro dominico”.

abschnitte.text: Eckhart was born around 1260 in Thuringia and entered the **Dominican** order. He studied and taught at the famous University of Paris. There he received the title of magister, which is where the name **Meister** (Master) Eckhart comes from. He also held important offices in the order and worked in Erfurt, Strasbourg and Cologne. He died in 1328, probably in Avignon.

Eckhart wrote his learned works in **Latin**, the language of the Church and the universities. Before nuns and ordinary people, however, he preached in **Middle High German**, the German language of his time. To express difficult thoughts, he coined many new words. That is why Eckhart is also important for the history of the German language.

Eckhart spoke of **detachment** (Abgeschiedenheit). By this he meant that a person becomes inwardly free from everything to which he clings, so that God can work in him. The innermost core of the soul he called the **little spark of the soul** (Seelenfünklein) or the ground of the soul. There, according to his teaching, the soul touches God. Many sermons are about the **birth of God in the soul**: God lets his Son come alive in the innermost being of a person.

Some statements of Eckhart sounded daring to churchmen. In Cologne proceedings were opened against him, and he appealed to the Pope in Avignon. After his death **Pope John XXII**, in 1329, with the bull **“In agro dominico”**, condemned 28 propositions as heretical or suspect. Even so, many people went on reading his texts, and his pupils spread his ideas.

gewusst: The title of the bull “In agro dominico” means “In the Lord's field”.
Even today people of different religions and many philosophers read the texts of Meister Eckhart.

teile.einleitung: Simon Peter was one of the twelve apostles and a close friend of Jesus. He was a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee before he followed Jesus. For the Catholic Church he is regarded as the first pope.
wichtigste: Peter was actually called Simon; Jesus gave him the new name.
Peter means “rock”.
His brother Andrew was also a fisherman and a disciple.
After Jesus was arrested, Peter said three times that he did not know him.
In pictures, Peter often carries keys.
St Peter's Basilica in Rome is named after him.

abschnitte.text: Simon was a **fisherman** on the Sea of Galilee, together with his brother **Andrew**. According to the Gospels, Jesus called the two of them with the words that they should now become fishers of men. They left their nets lying and followed him. Simon became one of the twelve apostles. Together with James and John he was one of the disciples closest to Jesus.

Jesus gave Simon a new name: **Cephas** in Aramaic, **Peter** in Greek. Both mean **rock**. Jesus said that he wanted to build his church on this rock. He also promised Peter the **keys of the kingdom of heaven**. That is why Peter is often painted with keys in art.

A well-known story tells how Jesus came to the disciples in the boat, walking on the water. Peter wanted to walk towards him and climbed out of the boat. For a few steps he managed it, but when he saw the strong wind he became **afraid** and began to sink. Jesus stretched out his hand and held him. The story shows Peter as brave, but also as a person with doubts.

Jesus had predicted that Peter would deny him before the **cock** crowed. After Jesus was arrested, Peter was asked whether he belonged to him. **Three times** he said out of fear that he did not know him. Then the cock crowed, and Peter remembered the words of Jesus. He went outside and wept bitterly.

After Easter, Peter became an important leader of the first Christians. According to tradition he later went to **Rome** and died there as a martyr. St Peter's Basilica in Vatican City is said to stand over his grave. According to Catholic teaching, Peter was the first Bishop of Rome and so the **first pope**. Protestant and Orthodox Christians also honour him, but see the office of pope differently.

gewusst: The feast day of Peter and Paul is on 29 June.
St Peter's Basilica is one of the largest churches in the world.

teile.einleitung: Paul of Tarsus was one of the most important people in the history of Christianity. At first he persecuted Christians, then he became one himself and travelled far to tell of the faith. His letters belong to the New Testament.
wichtigste: Paul was born in Tarsus, in the south of present-day Turkey.
At first he was called Saul and persecuted the Christians.
On the road to Damascus he had, according to the Bible, his conversion.
He earned his living as a tentmaker.
People count three missionary journeys, the first with Barnabas.
His first letter to the Thessalonians is regarded as the oldest document of the New Testament.
Because he evangelised mainly non-Jews, he is called the Apostle to the Gentiles.

abschnitte.text: Paul came from **Tarsus** in Cilicia, in the south of present-day **Turkey**. He was a Jew and bore the name **Saul**, in Greek form **Saulus**. Paul was his Roman name. He was a strictly observant Pharisee. He earned his living as a **tentmaker**. So later he did not have to let the communities pay him.

At first Paul **persecuted** the Christians. He wanted to have Christians arrested in **Damascus** too. On the way, according to the **Acts of the Apostles**, a bright light appeared to him, and he heard the voice of Jesus. Afterwards he was blind for a time. In Damascus he was baptised. The persecutor became one of the most zealous Christians. That is why people still say today: “to go from Saul to Paul”.

According to the Acts of the Apostles people count **three missionary journeys** through Asia Minor and Greece. On the first journey **Barnabas** accompanied him; it led among other places to Cyprus. In **Philippi** in Macedonia Paul founded the first Christian community in Europe. There the purple-dealer **Lydia** was baptised. In Athens he gave a speech on the **Areopagus** about the “unknown god”.

Paul saw himself above all as apostle to the **non-Jews**, whom people then called pagans. That is why he is also called the **Apostle to the Gentiles**. He taught that non-Jews too can become Christians without keeping all the Jewish laws. In the end Paul came to **Rome as a prisoner**. According to tradition he died there as a martyr.

Paul wrote **letters** to many communities in order to advise them from a distance. They are the oldest texts of the New Testament. The **first letter to the Thessalonians** is usually dated to about AD 50. It is therefore older than the Gospels. The letters of Paul have strongly shaped the Christian faith to this day.

gewusst: The saying “from Saul to Paul” means that someone completely changes his opinion.
According to the Acts of the Apostles, Paul possessed Roman citizenship.

teile.einleitung: The Ten Commandments are important rules from the Bible. According to the story, God gave them to Moses on Mount Sinai, written on two stone tablets. They are still very important in Judaism and Christianity today.
wichtigste: According to the Bible, God gave Moses ten commandments on the mountain.
Moses stayed on the mountain for 40 days and 40 nights.
The commandments were on two stone tablets.
The first commandment is: “You shall have no other gods before me.”
Other commandments require honouring one's parents and not stealing.
While Moses was away, the people made themselves a golden calf.

abschnitte.text: The Bible tells how the people of Israel left Egypt. On the way, **Moses** climbed **Mount Sinai**. There he stayed **40 days and 40 nights**, and God spoke with him. God gave him **ten commandments**. Moses carried **two stone tablets** down from the mountain, written on both sides.

The first commandments are about the relationship to God. The **first commandment** is: “You shall have no other gods before me.” So one should trust only the **one God**. Another commandment says that one should keep one day a week holy as a **day of rest**. In Judaism this is the **Sabbath**, in Christianity usually **Sunday**.

The other commandments regulate life with other people. One commandment is: “**Honour your father and your mother.**” To honour means to respect them. The commandment “You shall **not steal**” protects the property of others. Further commandments forbid, for example, killing or lying.

While Moses was on the mountain, the people became impatient. They cast a **calf** from gold jewellery and danced around it. When Moses came back and saw it, he became very angry. He **broke the tablets** at the foot of the mountain. Later he received new tablets.

The Ten Commandments are in the Bible in the **second Book of Moses** and once more in the **fifth Book of Moses**. Jews and Christians still learn them today. Many basic values of living together can be found in them. Many laws, too, contain the ban on theft and murder, for example.

gewusst: The Ten Commandments are also called the Decalogue, after the Greek word for “ten words”.
Jews, Catholics and Reformed Christians number the commandments slightly differently.

teile.einleitung: The Reformation Monument in Geneva recalls the Reformation, which strongly shaped the city in the 16th century. The long wall with large stone figures is one of the best-known monuments in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The monument stands in Geneva in the Parc des Bastions.
In the middle stand Farel, Calvin, Beza and Knox.
The wall is about 100 metres long.
Above it stands the motto “Post Tenebras Lux”.
The foundation stone was laid in 1909 for the 400th birthday of Calvin.
In 2002 Marie Dentière was honoured as the first woman with her name.

abschnitte.text: The **Reformation Monument** stands in **Geneva** in the **Parc des Bastions**, near the university. It is a wall about **100 metres** long. It stands on the site of the old city fortifications. In front of the wall lies a pool of water. The foundation stone was laid in **1909**, for the **400th birthday** of John Calvin.

In the middle stand four large stone figures: **William Farel**, **John Calvin**, **Theodore Beza** and **John Knox**. Farel brought the Reformation to Geneva. Calvin shaped the city with his teaching. Beza was his successor, and Knox carried the ideas to Scotland. To the right and left stand further figures from countries in which the Reformation spread.

Above the figures stands the Latin motto **“Post Tenebras Lux”**. That means “After darkness, light”. It is the motto of the city of Geneva and also appears in the Geneva coat of arms. The Reformers saw in their teaching a new light after a dark time.

Martin **Luther** and Huldrych **Zwingli** have no large statues. They are honoured with their **names carved in stone**. For a long time only men could be seen on the monument. In **2002** a woman was honoured with her name for the first time, **Marie Dentière**. In the 16th century she campaigned in Geneva for the Reformation and wrote about it.

gewusst: The four main figures are each about five metres tall.
The motto “Post Tenebras Lux” also stands on the coat of arms of the canton of Geneva.

teile.einleitung: The World Day of Prayer is an ecumenical day of prayer celebrated by Christian women all over the world. It takes place every year on the first Friday in March. Each year, women from a different country write the service.
wichtigste: The World Day of Prayer takes place on the first Friday in March.
It is prepared and shaped mainly by Christian women.
Each year the liturgy comes from a different country.
In 2025 it came from the Cook Islands, in 2026 from Nigeria.
The movement began in 1887 in the USA.
Since 1927 the day has been celebrated internationally and across denominations.

abschnitte.text: The **World Day of Prayer** traditionally takes place on the **first Friday in March**. On this day people in many countries celebrate the same service. Because the earth turns, the day begins in the Pacific and ends many hours later in America. In this way the prayer travels once around the world. Today the day is celebrated in over 120 countries.

The World Day of Prayer is a worldwide movement of **Christian women**. That is why it is also called the **Women's World Day of Prayer**. The women prepare and shape the services. Everyone may join in, including men and children.

**Ecumenism** means cooperation between the Christian denominations. At the World Day of Prayer, women of different denominations celebrate together. In Switzerland, Catholic, Reformed, Christian Catholic and free-church women take part. That is why the day is regarded as **ecumenical**.

The special feature is the **liturgy**, that is, the order of service. Each year women from a different country write the service. Everyone else celebrates it and gets to know the country. In 2025 the liturgy came from the **Cook Islands** in the South Pacific. In 2026 **Nigeria** was the focus, with the motto “Come! Bring your burdens”.

In **1887**, Christian women in the **USA** met for a day of prayer. From this the worldwide movement grew. In **1927** the first international, interdenominational World Day of Prayer took place. The **collection** on the World Day of Prayer is usually used for **projects for women and girls**. In this way prayer and action go together.

gewusst: The guiding motto of the World Day of Prayer is “Informed prayer, prayerful action”.
The Cook Islands lie in the middle of the Pacific, between New Zealand and Hawaii.

teile.einleitung: The Christmas story tells of the birth of Jesus in Bethlehem. Best known is the version from the Gospel of Luke with the manger, the shepherds and the angels. Christians all over the world remember it at Christmas.
wichtigste: The best-known version is in the Gospel of Luke, in chapter two.
Emperor Augustus ordered a census.
That is why Mary and Joseph travelled to Bethlehem.
There was no room for them in the inn.
Mary laid the child in a manger.
An angel announced to the shepherds that the Saviour was born.

abschnitte.text: In the **Gospel of Luke** it says that the Roman Emperor **Augustus** ordered that all the people in his empire be counted. Everyone was to register in the town of their ancestors. **Joseph** came from the family of King David. That is why he had to travel with **Mary** from Nazareth to **Bethlehem**.

In Bethlehem the **inn** was full. There was no room for Mary and Joseph. So the child was born among the animals. Mary wrapped him in swaddling clothes and laid him in a **manger**. A manger is a feeding trough for animals.

In the night an angel appeared to **shepherds** in the field. He said that the **Saviour** was born. In older Bibles the word used is **Heiland**, an old German word for Saviour. The shepherds set off and found the child in the manger. Afterwards they told everyone about it.

The **Gospel of Matthew** also tells of the birth of Jesus. There **wise men** from the East follow a star and bring gifts: gold, frankincense and myrrh. The shepherds, on the other hand, appear only in **Luke**. In nativity scenes and nativity plays both stories are often shown together.

The name **Bethlehem** comes from Hebrew and means “**house of bread**”. The town lies south of Jerusalem. There stands the **Church of the Nativity**, one of the oldest churches in the world. It stands at the place where people imagine the birth of Jesus took place. Every year many pilgrims visit this church.

gewusst: In the Church of the Nativity, a silver star marks the place where Jesus is said to have been born.
In Switzerland the wise men are celebrated on 6 January as the Three Kings, with the Three Kings' cake.

teile.einleitung: Saint Lucia lived long ago in Syracuse in Sicily. Her feast on 13 December brings light into the dark Advent season and is celebrated above all in Sweden.
wichtigste: Lucia Day is on 13 December.
Lucia came from Syracuse in Sicily.
Her name has to do with the Latin word lux, light.
